The test image shows a corn stalk split open longitudinally, revealing shredded fibrous interior with vascular strands and rotted pith. This is a stem. Top candidates from the stem category: Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback.

Now viewing one reference per candidate before deciding:

Charcoal Stalk Rot reference shows dark gray/charred internal tissue with sclerotia. The test image is much lighter (tan/straw colored) without the dark charred appearance. Let me check Diplodia Stalk Rot.
Diplodia Stalk Rot reference shows a lodged stalk at a node, not matching the shredded internal appearance. Now checking Physoderma_Stalk_Rot.

Physoderma Stalk Rot shows dark spots on exterior of a green stalk - doesn't match. I've used all 4 reference views.

**Analysis summary:**
- Test image: corn stalk split open longitudinally showing shredded interior with only fibrous vascular strands remaining, tan/straw colored, pith completely disintegrated
- Charcoal Stalk Rot reference: closest match - shredded pith with vascular strands exposed (though reference is darker/charred)
- Diplodia Stalk Rot: external lodged stalk view, no internal shredding
- Physoderma Stalk Rot: external dark spots on green stalk, no match

The shredded stalk appearance with pith rotted away leaving only stringy vascular bundles is the hallmark of Charcoal Stalk Rot. The lighter tan color in the test image may reflect an earlier stage or different lighting conditions. No other stem disease in this set produces this characteristic shredded internal morphology.
